items.text: An MPT costs two years and a fee.
The MPT is a two-year postgraduate degree in one specialty.
Often clinic-based, so you can set a fee and build repeat patients.
Who pays you Patients per session, or a clinic or hospital as employer.
Answer the four questions to decide whether the MPT suits you, then pass the three proofs before you ask patients or an employer to pay for your specialty.
Spend a few shifts in stroke and spinal rehab, a sports clinic and a child therapy unit before you choose.
Add the fee, travel and the salary you give up during a full-time course.

blocks.heading: Growth, Scale and AI for MPT Physiotherapists

items.text: A salaried physiotherapy job has a pay ceiling set by the employer, so growth comes from what you own: a practice in one track, a home-visit service, tele-rehab, or injury-prevention talks sold to gyms and schools.
Choosing one track, building case proof and growing a referral network are the decisions that unlock high income opportunities.
The ownership path: a practice or home-visit service in one track scales because you set the fee, can add therapists and can build repeat patients.

blocks.heading: Government Post Pays By the Pay

figures.label: Monthly Pay Allowance
figures.source: A government post pays by the pay level of that post, not by your degree. The Delhi draft rule puts the physiotherapist at Level 6, which is Rs 35,400 to Rs 1,12,400 a month in basic pay before allowances. Read the qualification line in the exact notice before you apply.
